newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan charges Chung-hsin, regulators with graft.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan charges Chung-hsin, regulators with graft.

text.p: Taiwan on Monday charged nine officials from the government and Chung-hsin Electric, including the firm's former chairman, accusing them of involvement in a T$435 million construction project scandal.

Chung-hsin ex-chairman Huang Chung and others are suspected of receiving kickbacks after Chung-hsin won bids to build two furnaces for T$1.35 billion in the southern Taiwan towns of Tainan and Chiayi in 1993, prosecutors said.
"Nine officials, including Huang Chung, have been charged with corruption in this case," Huang Wen-lee, a Taipei district court prosecutor, said on state television.
Also charged were Hsieh Jin-song, deputy director of the Department of Environmental Protection, and former department commissioner Li Kung-cheh, state television reported.

The court said that government and Chung-hsin officials conspired to subcontract the two projects to other firms for T$900 million after Chung-hsin had won the bids with T$1.35 billion -- sharing the difference of T$435 million.
Huang Chung alone was accused of receiving T$50 million of the difference, the court added.
Prosecutor Huang did not say when the case would go to trial.
Chung-hsin, one of Taiwan's leading electrical appliance makers, has incurred serious financial losses from the two furnaces and other recent construction projects.
The company reported a net loss of T$3.155 billion in the first six months of 1996 and a net loss of T$991 million for 1995.
